findings.reason: the deliverable's interface must be restated (a per-iteration path provider, or the advancement kept in the caller) before a builder can consolidate without silently changing resumption's attempt numbering.
findings.text: the shared function is specified to take "the claim path, the record to write and a staleness predicate", but claim_next_attempt derives its path from a per-iteration variable (`path = attempt_claim_path(run_id, claimed)`, reckon/crew/resumption.py:391) and after a reclaim advances it (`if current > claimed: claimed = current + 1`, resumption.py:401-405); a single fixed path plus a boolean predicate cannot express that, so a builder implementing the interface as written drops the advancement and re-creates a claim at a superseded attempt number, contradicting §16's "Neither caller changes its behaviour" — and no test covers the branch (tests/test_a_resume_never_launches_beside_another_node.py:317-337 passes a record at attempt 1 with a claim at attempt 2, so current ≤ claimed in every case), so §16's own "§11's tests pass unchanged" control would not catch the loss.

response_events.reason: the section is deferred rather than built: four content reviews found the two claims share only the exclusive os.open call, while their paths, loops and staleness rules differ (the attempt claim re-derives its path and advances its number after a reclaim), so one shared function would carry two interfaces and risk the behaviour change the section forbids; the reuse finding is exempted with this reason
